mcq_fix.s: Consider the following pairs: a. Mohenjodaro — Citadel and lower town b. Harappa — Citadel and lower town c. Kalibangan — Citadel and fortified lower town d. Lothal — Citadel and lower town in one enclosure e. Sutkagendor — Citadel and lower city Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
o: a, b, c, d and e
mcq_fix.why: duplicate label 'a' in stem; relabelled a-e

mcq_drop.why: dubious trivia ('first artefact reported from Harappa')

pyq_bad.why: wrong topic: colonial urban administration (Lottery Committee, Calcutta)
suspect key: IVC has no identified buildings of worship; burnt-brick buildings expected

patterns: Site-identification is the dominant shape: Great Bath / Great Granary / most wells -> Mohenjodaro; three-part city -> Dholavira; port/dockyard -> Lothal; water management -> Dholavira.
Statement traps from CGPSC 2022: same brick size for all constructions and mostly single-storey houses are false; 10 m main streets true.
APPSC asks the hallmark (town planning) and the great granary site; little depth beyond that.
App has many multi-statement items on drainage, bricks and Dholavira that are deeper but sound; a few Harappa find-trivia items exceed PYQ depth.
